subject: Human Body
title: The Pineal Gland and Melatonin
description: A quick, practical guide to The Pineal Gland and Melatonin.

hook.text: As darkness falls, a rice-grain-sized gland in your brain starts releasing melatonin. Sleep is coming.

buildup.text: The pineal gland responds to light signals from the eyes. Darkness triggers melatonin; light suppresses it.

discovery.text: Melatonin doesn't put you to sleep directly.

twist.text: Blue light from screens suppresses melatonin production.

climax.text: The pineal gland is your internal clock's chemical arm.

punchline.text: Your phone's blue light fights your sleep hormone every night.

quiz.question: How does blue light from screens affect melatonin?
options: It increases melatonin to help you sleep
It has no effect on melatonin production
It suppresses melatonin, fooling the brain into thinking it's daytime
